mainTopic: Testing whether a secondary holy item can be stricter than its source, and the sources that an אשם must be slaughtered in the צפון
overview: The amud opens by testing a rule from the ongoing discussion: something that gets its holiness from another holy thing is never stricter than its source. The גמרא raises three cases that seem to break this rule: food bought with מעשר שני money, a תמורה, and the leftover of a פסח. Each is answered by showing the difference has another reason, such as weak holiness, a holy source, or the animal having become a שלמים. The גמרא then gives a second source that a עולה slaughtered outside the צפון is invalid: the repeated word העולה. Next it asks how we know an אשם needs the צפון, and learns the שחיטה, the קבלה and the collector's own position from ויקרא 7:2. To show the rule is required and not just ideal, it brings ויקרא 14:13 about the מצורע's אשם. That פסוק seems to be needed to bring the מצורע's אשם back to its normal rules, but the גמרא answers that writing the צפון rule twice shows it is required. The amud ends by starting to ask whether this answer works under every view of יצא לידון בדבר החדש, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that מעשר שני itself can be redeemed, but food bought with מעשר money cannot be. That looks like the secondary item is stricter than the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at מעשר: it can be redeemed, while food bought with מעשר money cannot be redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a case that seems to break the rule that the secondary item is never stricter than the source. The proof for this case comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original מעשר שני produce can be redeemed, meaning its holiness is moved onto coins. Food that was bought with those coins is only a 'second-generation' holy item, yet it seems to be harder to redeem. If that is true, the secondary item is stricter than the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני: produce eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Is redeemed (its holiness moves onto money)
Something bought with מעשר שני money
But look at...: opens a challenge from a case

phrases.english: But there is tithe, which can be redeemed,
whereas what is bought with tithe money
cannot be redeemed –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule from the ongoing discussion against a new case
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a secondary holy item is never stricter than its source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food bought with מעשר money seems harder to redeem than the מעשר itself, so the secondary item seems stricter

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about impure bought food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: bought food that became impure must be redeemed, and רבי יהודה says it must be buried. It reads in: only once it is impure can it be redeemed, not before.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: food bought with מעשר money that became impure must be redeemed. רבי יהודה says: it must be buried. So if it became impure, yes, it can be redeemed; if it did not become impure, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim from step 1 by quoting a משנה and drawing an inference from its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only allows redeeming the bought food after it becomes impure, which shows that pure bought food cannot be redeemed. Original מעשר can be redeemed even when pure. According to רבי יהודה, the bought food cannot be redeemed even when impure and must be buried, so it looks even stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: Became ritually impure
It must be buried
Yes... no: an inference from the exact wording

phrases.english: As we learned: what was bought with tithe money
that became impure must be redeemed.
Rabbi Yehuda says: it must be buried.
If it became impure, yes; if it did not become impure, no!
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא reading into the משנה: pure bought food cannot be redeemed at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That food bought with מעשר money cannot be redeemed (when pure, and according to רבי יהודה not even when impure)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in מעשר שני, plus an inference from its wording

steps.title: Its holiness is too weak to pass on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bought food is not stricter. Its holiness is simply too weak to move onto redemption money.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, its holiness is not strong enough to take hold of its redemption money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a different reason why the bought food cannot be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming means moving holiness from the item onto money. Bought food has only second-hand holiness, which is too weak to jump to yet another item. So the reason it cannot be redeemed is weakness, not strictness, and the rule stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
Is strong
Its holiness
To take hold of its redemption money

steps.confusionAlert: Being unable to be redeemed sounds like a stricter law, but here it comes from weaker holiness, not stronger.

phrases.english: There, its holiness is not strong enough
to take hold of its redemption money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1 and 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the law (weak holiness, not strictness)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bought food is stricter than מעשר because it cannot be redeemed
steps.terutzMaskana: Bought food cannot be redeemed because its weak holiness cannot move onto money, so it is not truly stricter

steps.title: Challenge from a substitute animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new case: הקדש does not take hold on a permanently blemished animal, yet תמורה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at תמורה: הקדש does not take effect on an animal with a permanent blemish, while תמורה does take effect!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second case that seems to show a secondary holy item is stricter than its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה gets its holiness from the original קרבן, so it is the secondary item. Yet its holiness takes hold on a permanently blemished animal, where regular הקדש does not fully take hold. That makes the secondary item look stronger and stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal swapped for a קרבן, which becomes holy too
Consecrated animals or offerings
Take effect
An animal with a permanent blemish

phrases.english: But there is a substitute animal –
for consecration does not take effect
on a permanently blemished animal,
phrases.notes: He means the animal itself does not become fully holy like a קרבן.

phrases.english: while it, the substitute, does take effect!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is answered, a new challenge to the same rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a secondary holy item is never stricter than its source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תמורה takes hold where regular הקדש does not, so the secondary item seems stronger than the source

steps.title: Substitute draws power from holy, not ordinary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a תמורה comes from an already holy animal, while regular הקדש starts from a plain, unholy animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תמורה comes through the power of a holy animal, while הקדש comes through the power of an ordinary animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the תמורה challenge by explaining where each kind of holiness comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular הקדש starts from ordinary חולין, so it is too weak to fully take hold on a blemished animal. A תמורה flows from a קרבן that is already holy, so it carries stronger force. The difference comes from the strength of the source, so the challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the power of
Ordinary, non-holy items or animals
Comes from

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges are answered with the same idea: how strong the holiness is depends on where it comes from. Bought food has weak second-hand holiness, while a תמורה draws on an already holy animal.

phrases.english: A substitute comes through the power of a holy animal,
but consecrated animals come through the power of ordinary animals.
phrases.notes: Some versions say קָאָתֵי (round brackets), and the corrected wording is the plural קָאָתוּ (square brackets). The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by the source of their holiness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תמורה is stronger than its source קרבן, breaking the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: תמורה draws from an already holy animal, while הקדש starts from חולין, so the comparison does not break the rule

steps.title: The leftover of a פסח seems stricter than the פסח itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule again: a פסח needs no סמיכה, נסכים, or תנופה, but its leftover animal needs all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the פסח. It does not need hands placed on it, wine libations, or waving of the breast and thigh. Yet its leftover animal does need hands placed on it, libations, and waving of the breast and thigh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case where the secondary item looks stricter than the original. It challenges the idea that this never happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal set aside for a פסח that was not offered in time is brought as a leftover offering. That leftover needs סמיכה, נסכים, and תנופת חזה ושוק, while the real פסח needs none of these. So the 'child' seems to have more rules than the 'parent.'

keyTerms.meaning: The Passover offering
Pressing one's hands on the animal's head before slaughter
Wine libations brought with an offering
Waving the breast and thigh of the animal
The leftover; an animal set aside for a פסח that was not used for it

phrases.english: But there is the Paschal offering,
which does not require placing of hands
or libations, or waving of the breast and thigh,
whereas its leftover
phrases.notes: This is an animal set aside as a פסח that was not offered at the right time.

phrases.english: requires placing of hands
and libations and waving of the breast and thigh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תמורה case was answered, the גמרא raises another case against the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a secondary item is never stricter than its original
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The leftover of a פסח has three requirements the פסח itself lacks, so the secondary looks stricter.

steps.title: Outside its time, a פסח is simply a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פסח during the rest of the year is a שלמים, so it follows שלמים rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסח during the rest of the days of the year is a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The leftover is not a stricter 'secondary פסח'; it has simply become a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once its time has passed, the animal is no longer treated as a פסח at all. It is a regular שלמים, and a שלמים needs סמיכה, נסכים, and תנופה. So there is no case here of a secondary item being stricter than its original.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offering
The rest of the days of the year

steps.whatToRemember: The rule stands: a secondary item is not stricter than its original. The leftover of a פסח only looks stricter because it has actually become a שלמים.

phrases.english: A Paschal offering on the rest of the days of the year
is a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֶּסַח בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה שְׁלָמִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the leftover belongs to a different category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leftover is a secondary form of פסח that is stricter than the פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leftover is a full שלמים with all שלמים rules, so it is not a stricter version of the פסח.

steps.title: Another source: the repeated word 'the burnt offering' means it must stay in its place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different source that a עולה not slaughtered in the צפון is invalid: the repeated word העולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: the פסוק says 'the burnt offering,' to teach that it must be in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate source that a עולה is invalid if it is not slaughtered in the צפון. This one does not depend on learning from the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the place of the עולה' already appeared in an earlier פסוק. Saying 'העולה' again shows that its place is required, so a עולה slaughtered elsewhere is invalid. This source avoids the whole discussion about whether a secondary item can be stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another answer or source
Burnt offering
It shall be in its place

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
The verse states: "the burnt offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:29. The same words already appeared in ויקרא 4:24, so saying them again teaches something new.

phrases.english: it shall be in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the first method, the גמרא gives a second source for the same law.
steps.raayaObject: That a עולה not slaughtered in the צפון is invalid even after the fact
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repeated word העולה in ויקרא 4:29

steps.title: Where do we learn that an אשם needs the צפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that an אשם must be slaughtered in the צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that an אשם needs the צפון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks for the source that an אשם must be slaughtered in the צפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the discussion was about the עולה and the חטאת. Now the גמרא turns to the אשם, another of the most holy offerings, and asks where its צפון requirement comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
From where do we know?
The north side of the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: A guilt offering, from where do we derive
that it requires the north?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the עולה to a new offering, the אשם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that an אשם must be slaughtered in the צפון

steps.title: The אשם is slaughtered where the עולה is slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from a פסוק that the אשם is slaughtered in the same place as the עולה, which is the צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they shall slaughter the guilt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. The אשם is slaughtered in the same place as the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the עולה must be slaughtered in the צפון. The פסוק ties the אשם to the place of the עולה, so the אשם also needs the צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
They shall slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם needs the צפון because the תורה links its place of slaughter to the place of the עולה.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering
they shall slaughter the guilt offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁחֲטוּ אֶת הָעֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ויקרא 7:2 places the אשם's slaughter where the עולה is slaughtered, which is the צפון.

steps.title: Where does the collection of the blood happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has a source that the אשם is slaughtered in the צפון. Now it asks for a source that the blood is also collected there.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the slaughtering. Where do we learn the rule for the collecting of the blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pleased with its source for שחיטה in the צפון. It now asks about the next stage of the offering, the קבלה (collecting the blood in a vessel).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in Step 10 talked about slaughtering. Collecting the blood is a separate service, so it needs its own source. The גמרא is checking whether the צפון rule covers that stage too.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
Slaughtering the animal
Collecting the blood in a vessel
From where do we know?

phrases.english: We have found a source for slaughtering,
phrases.notes: He means the source from Step 10, that the אשם is slaughtered in the צפון.

phrases.english: from where do we know the rule for collecting the blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the צפון rule from Step 10 to the next service.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the קבלה of an אשם must be in the צפון.

steps.title: The words about the blood include the collection
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק continues with 'and its blood shall be sprinkled,' which teaches that the collecting of its blood is also in the צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and its blood he shall sprinkle.' This teaches that collecting its blood is also in the צפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the end of the same פסוק, which mentions the blood right after the slaughtering. This places the collecting of the blood in the צפון as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the blood to the place of slaughter. The blood is collected right after the שחיטה and before it is sprinkled, so the collecting belongs to the same place, the צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall sprinkle or throw (the blood on the מזבח)
Receiving or collecting (the blood)
The northern part of the עזרה
Also

phrases.english: "And its blood he shall sprinkle":
the collecting of its blood is also in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'ואת דמו יזרוק' in the same פסוק places the קבלה in the צפון too.

steps.title: Must the collector himself stand in the north?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the כהן who collects the blood must himself be standing in the צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that the person collecting the blood must himself be in the צפון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows the blood is collected in the צפון. It asks a sharper question: must the כהן doing the collecting also stand in the צפון?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that the blood and the vessel are in the צפון does not settle where the כהן himself must stand. He could be standing just outside the צפון and reaching in. The גמרא wants a source that covers the כהן's own position.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who collects the blood
Himself

phrases.english: From where do we know the rule for the collector himself?
phrases.notes: He means that the כהן's own body must be standing in the צפון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines Step 12 by moving from the blood to the person collecting it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the כהן collecting the blood must himself stand in the צפון.

steps.title: The extra word adds the collector
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said just 'its blood,' but it says 'and its blood.' That extra wording includes the collector himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could have said 'its blood,' but it says 'and its blood.' The extra wording teaches the rule for the collector.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the extra wording 'and' in 'and its blood.' That extra wording teaches that the collector must also be in the צפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just 'דמו' would have been enough to teach the collecting of the blood, as in Step 12. The added 'ואת' is extra, so the גמרא uses it to include something more: the כהן doing the collecting.

keyTerms.meaning: Its blood
'And' plus the word את; extra wording that comes to include something

phrases.english: Not just "its blood" but "and its blood."
phrases.notes: The extra 'ואת' isn't needed for the simple meaning, so it comes to include the collector.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'ואת' in 'ואת דמו' includes the מקבל himself.

steps.title: Is the north rule required or only the ideal?
steps.stepSummary: The sources so far show that the צפון is the proper way. The גמרא asks for a source that the offering is invalid if this was not done.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that it is the proper way to do the מצוה. From where do we know that it is required, so the offering is invalid without it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the צפון is the right place לכתחילה. Now it asks whether doing it elsewhere disqualifies the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many rules in קדשים are only למצוה, meaning the best way, and the offering still works if they were not kept. A rule that is לעכב makes the offering invalid without it. The פסוק so far proves only the first level, so the גמרא wants proof of the second.

keyTerms.meaning: As the proper, ideal way, but not required after the fact
Required; without it the offering is invalid

steps.confusionAlert: 'למצוה' does not mean the rule is unimportant. It means the offering would still count בדיעבד if the rule was missed. 'לעכב' means it would not count.

phrases.english: We have found that it is the proper way to do the מצוה,
from where do we know that it is required, so the offering is invalid without it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the level of the question from 'proper way' to 'required'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that an אשם not offered in the צפון is invalid.

steps.title: Another verse makes the rule required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another פסוק about an אשם: 'And he shall slaughter the sheep' in the place where the חטאת and עולה are slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another פסוק is written: 'And he shall slaughter the sheep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a second פסוק about slaughtering an אשם in the place of the חטאת and עולה. Because the תורה repeats the rule, it becomes required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the rule a second time shows the תורה insists on it. So the צפון is not just the ideal for an אשם. Without it, the offering is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Another פסוק
Sheep (here, the animal brought as an אשם)

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
"And he shall slaughter the sheep."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:13. It goes on: in the place where the חטאת and עולה are slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא כְּתִיב: וְשָׁחַט אֶת הַכֶּבֶשׂ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated instruction in ויקרא 14:13 makes the צפון required (לעכב) for an אשם.

steps.title: That verse is already needed for another rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 16. The פסוק 'ושחט את הכבש' is already needed for a rule taught in a ברייתא: something taken out of its general category to teach a new rule stays out until the Torah clearly puts it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this פסוק really come to teach this? It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: Something that was included in a general category but was taken out to teach a new rule, you may not return it to its general category until the פסוק clearly returns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 16. It says the פסוק has a different job, based on a known principle from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle says: once the תורה gives one case special new rules, that case is treated as separate from its group. It goes back to the group's rules only if a פסוק says so. The גמרא claims 'ושחט את הכבש' is exactly that kind of פסוק, putting this אשם back with all other אשמות. If so, it is used up and cannot also teach that the צפון is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this really come for this purpose? (a challenge)
It is needed (for something else)
A general category or group
A new rule special to this case
Clearly, explicitly

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of how the תורה is learned: one פסוק generally cannot serve two jobs. If a פסוק is already used for one rule, the גמרא must find a way to learn the second rule from it, or find another source.

phrases.english: But does this verse come for this purpose?!
This verse is needed for that which was taught in a baraita:
A matter that was included in a general category
and went out to be judged with a new rule,
phrases.notes: The Torah gave this one case a special rule that the rest of its group doesn't have.

phrases.english: you are not permitted to return it to its general category
until the verse returns it to its general category explicitly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'ושחט את הכבש' (ויקרא 14:13) to prove that the צפון is required for an אשם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already needed to return a case that was taken out of its category back to its category, following the ברייתא's principle. A פסוק that is already used for that job cannot also teach that the צפון is required.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks why the extra words 'like the חטאת is the אשם' are needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the מצורע's אשם and asks why it says 'כחטאת האשם' when the פסוק already compared the אשם to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does that work? The פסוק says: 'And he shall slaughter the sheep in the place where he slaughters the חטאת and the עולה, in the holy place, for like the חטאת is the אשם.' The פסוק did not need to say 'like the חטאת is the אשם.' So why does it say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now showing the ברייתא it mentioned in Step 17. The ברייתא opens by asking why the פסוק adds the words 'כחטאת האשם.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק already ties the אשם to the חטאת by saying they are slaughtered in the same place. So the words 'like the חטאת is the אשם' look extra. The ברייתא is setting up its answer, which comes in the next step.

steps.title: The מצורע's אשם is brought back to the normal rules of blood and fats
steps.stepSummary: The מצורע's אשם has a special new rule, so we might think it skips the normal service on the מזבח. 'כחטאת האשם' teaches that it still needs its blood placed on the מזבח and its fats burned there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצורע's אשם was taken out of the general group to teach a new rule: its blood is put on the thumb, the big toe and the right ear. So you might think it does not need its blood placed on the מזבח or its fats burned there. That is why the פסוק says 'like the חטאת is the אשם.' Just as a חטאת needs its blood placed and its fats burned on the מזבח, so too the מצורע's אשם needs its blood placed and its fats burned on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The extra words bring the מצורע's אשם back under the normal rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This applies the rule from Step 17: something taken out of its group to teach a new rule stays out until the תורה clearly puts it back. The special rule about the thumb, toe and ear took the מצורע's אשם out, so the פסוק must bring it back. In the same way, 'ושחט את הכבש' is needed to bring back slaughter in the צפון for the מצורע's אשם. That leaves no extra wording to teach that the offering is invalid.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the מצורע's אשם stops being an אשם. It has one special rule added, and the פסוק makes sure the normal rules still apply to it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the challenge in Step 17. Since the מצורע's פסוק is already used to bring back the normal rules, it seems it cannot also prove that the offering is invalid without the צפון.

steps.title: Writing the צפון rule twice shows the offering is invalid without it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers Step 17: if the צפון were only the proper way, the תורה would write it in one place and learn the other from it. Writing it in both places shows the offering is invalid without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written it in this place and not in that place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 17. The rule of slaughtering in the צפון is written twice, and that repetition is the source that the offering is invalid without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the צפון were only the proper way, one mention would be enough, and the other kind of אשם could learn from it. Since the תורה writes the rule for the מצורע's אשם and also for the regular אשם, one mention is extra. That extra mention teaches that the offering is invalid if it was not slaughtered in the צפון.

steps.title: The answer works only under one view of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the previous answer is fine if we hold that only the item taken out to teach a new rule cannot learn from its general category. This prepares a challenge from the other view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well if we hold that when something is taken out of its category to teach a new rule, it is only that item itself which does not learn rules from its general category.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to the answer in Step 20. It says the answer fits well under one way of understanding the rule of יצא לידון בדבר החדש, which hints that under another way it may not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 17 says something pulled out of its category to teach a new rule stays out until the תורה puts it back. Here the גמרא points to the narrower version: only the item that was pulled out cannot learn from its category. The word הָנִיחָא tells us a 'but' is coming, and the next line, on the next amud, will ask what happens under a broader version of the rule.
